entities.name: Afdal al-Din al-Khunaji
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Afḍal al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Nāmāwar ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Khūnajī, best known as Afḍal al-Dīn Khūnajī, was a Persian scholar and a judge (qadi) in Ayyubid Egypt, whose work in logic and jurisprudence would have a lasting impact on Islamic scholarship.

As a prominent figure in 13th-century Ayyubid Egypt, Afḍal al-Dīn Khūnajī was deeply involved in the intellectual and religious life of the region, collaborating with other prominent scholars such as Ibn Rushd and Ibn Taymiyyah.

His legacy extends beyond his own era, as his writings on logic and jurisprudence influenced the development of Islamic thought in the Middle Ages, shaping the intellectual landscape of the Islamic world for centuries to come.

The exact date of his birth is unknown, but his death in 1248 marks the end of an era in the life of this influential scholar, whose contributions to Islamic scholarship continue to be studied and debated by scholars today.
